title: Research and Analysis with Claude
description: Use Claude's reasoning and large context window to conduct research, synthesize information, and produce structured analysis.

data.text: Claude is a powerful research assistant — not because it searches the web (it does not, by default), but because it excels at synthesizing information from documents you provide and reasoning through complex questions carefully. For fact-checking or live research, pair Claude with Perplexity. For deep analysis of documents, datasets, and long-form content, Claude is the superior tool.

data.title: A structured research workflow:
items: Gather your source materials (PDFs, articles, data files, notes)
Upload the most relevant documents to a Claude conversation
Ask Claude to summarize and identify key themes
Request specific analysis — patterns, gaps, contradictions
Ask Claude to structure findings into a report or outline
Validate key claims against your source material

data.text: Using Claude's Context Window for Research

Claude's 200K token context window is a research superpower. You can upload an entire book, a legal brief, a research paper collection, or a large dataset and ask Claude to analyze it holistically. Unlike tools that process documents in chunks, Claude can cross-reference information across the entire document set.

data.title: Research tasks Claude handles well:
items: Summarizing multiple research papers and identifying consensus
Extracting data points and trends from reports
Identifying gaps or contradictions in a body of work
Creating literature reviews from uploaded papers
Synthesizing interview transcripts or meeting notes

data.text: Research prompts should specify the scope, the sources (if uploaded), and the output format. Instead of 'what do these papers say about X?', try 'Review the three uploaded papers on climate policy. For each paper, identify: 1) the main argument, 2) the methodology, 3) key findings, 4) limitations acknowledged by the authors. Then synthesize: where do they agree, and where do they conflict?'

data.title: Research prompt example
data.content: Prompt: 'I have uploaded three annual reports from competing companies in the sustainable packaging space. For each company, extract their revenue figures, sustainability commitments, and market positioning. Then create a comparison table and write a 200-word analysis of who is leading and why. Focus on concrete commitments, not marketing language.'

data.title: Critical steps for reliable research:
items: Cross-check key statistics and facts against your source documents
Verify that Claude did not confuse details between different sources
Ask Claude to cite which document each claim comes from
Spot-check specific pages or sections Claude references
Be skeptical of any 'facts' Claude states without a source in your uploaded material

data.title: Claude can hallucinate details
data.text: Like all LLMs, Claude can sometimes fabricate plausible-sounding details — especially for factual claims not found in your source material. Always verify important statistics, quotes, dates, and specific claims. Use Claude for synthesis and pattern detection, not as a primary source of facts.

data.title: Research with Claude
points: Upload source documents and ask for structured analysis
Use the 200K context window to analyze multiple documents together
Specify output format — tables, bullet points, structured reports
Always validate key claims against your original sources
Pair Claude with Perplexity for live research and citations
